subject.title: iOS app: push notifications for assistant messages + background Talk mode

question: Should native iOS assistant-message APNs delivery and background Talk continuation be product-supported now, and what privacy and opt-in boundaries should they use?
rationale: The APNs relay, registration, local notification, and background audio pieces exist, but payload content, lock-screen exposure, per-node opt-in, tap routing, duplicate foreground behavior, and background microphone policy require maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Approve scoped generic alerts first
options.body: Add a dedicated assistant-reply APNs kind with generic notification text by default, explicit preview opt-in if desired, and keep background Talk governed by the existing explicit background-listening control until live proof is accepted.

options.title: Split the product decisions
options.body: Track assistant-message APNs and background Talk as separate design items so the lower-risk notification route can move independently from background microphone policy.

options.title: Defer native support
options.body: Keep native iOS behavior foreground-first and rely on third-party channels until maintainers approve a broader mobile notification and background-audio privacy model.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped generic alerts first
recommendation.body: Add a dedicated assistant-reply APNs kind with generic notification text by default, explicit preview opt-in if desired, and keep background Talk governed by the existing explicit background-listening control until live proof is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a user-facing iOS privacy/product contract choice, and steipete has recent merged iOS Talk, chat, and multi-gateway product-surface work.
